submissions.behaviourOfInterest: How value realization in an open loyalty system can accelerate—and constrain—itself over time.

variables.label: Relevant, visible opportunities
variables.definition: Worthwhile opportunities that an eligible member can discover and understand.

variables.label: Opportunity capture
variables.definition: The rate at which members act on worthwhile, eligible opportunities.

variables.label: Member value-realization rate
variables.definition: The proportion of worthwhile, eligible value entering the chain that becomes a fulfilled benefit the member can actually use.

variables.label: Program trust
variables.definition: Confidence that the program will reliably convert its promises into usable value.

variables.label: Repeat participation
variables.definition: The continuation of relevant earning, redemption, and benefit-use behaviours over time.

variables.label: Outcome information
variables.definition: Usable information about what value members pursued, received, and ultimately realized.

variables.label: Decisioning quality
variables.definition: The system's ability to select more relevant opportunities using observed outcomes.

variables.label: Reward-processing demand
variables.definition: The volume and complexity of earning, posting, redemption, fulfilment, and support activity.

variables.label: Operational load
variables.definition: The workload placed on the capabilities and teams responsible for delivering program value.

variables.label: Value friction
variables.definition: Delays, errors, effort, and breakdowns that obstruct progress from available value to realized value.

links.mechanism: Relevant, understandable opportunities are more likely to be pursued and successfully earned.
More worthwhile value captured creates more value capable of being fulfilled and realized.
Repeated successful delivery gradually builds confidence in the program.
Higher trust increases members' willingness to participate again.
Participation creates outcome signals about what members pursue, receive, ignore, or struggle with.
Usable outcomes improve learning after analysis, decision updates, and organizational action.
Better decisions improve opportunity selection, timing, eligibility, and delivery context.
More participation produces more transactions, qualifications, fulfilments, and possible exceptions.
Demand increases operational load when capacity and coordination do not scale proportionately.
Capacity pressure and weak coordination tend to increase backlogs, delays, errors, and unresolved cases.
Failures prevent worthwhile value from becoming a successfully fulfilled benefit.

loops.name: Value Realization and Learning Flywheel
loops.summary: Reliable realization can build trust and participation, producing the outcome information required to improve future decisions.
loops.behaviourOverTime: Compounding growth or compounding decline, depending on direction of travel.
narrative: As decision relevance and opportunity visibility improve, members capture more worthwhile opportunities. Greater capture increases successful value realization. Repeated realization builds trust, which supports continued participation. Participation generates richer evidence about what members pursue, earn, redeem, realize, ignore, or struggle with. When that outcome information improves decisioning, future opportunities become more relevant and visible.

The loop can also move downward: poor relevance can reduce opportunity capture and realization, weakening trust, participation, outcome information, and future decisioning. This is a learning loop organized around realized outcomes—not simply offer personalization.

loops.name: Operational Friction and Capacity Constraint
loops.summary: Participation can increase processing demand and operational load, creating friction that reduces realized value and eventually constrains participation.
loops.behaviourOverTime: A ceiling on participation and realized value that tightens as volume grows.
narrative: As repeat participation increases, more reward events must be qualified, posted, redeemed, fulfilled, explained, and supported. If this demand grows faster than effective operational capacity, delays, errors, and unresolved exceptions increase. These failures reduce successful value realization, weaken trust, and eventually constrain participation.
Balancing does not mean beneficial. This loop can impose a ceiling on participation and value realization.

leveragePoints.title: Shared value-state information
leveragePoints.mechanism: Create a reliable view of what is identified, eligible, pursued, qualified, earned, pending, posted, redeemed, fulfilled, or unresolved.
leveragePoints.signal: The system cannot improve value realization when members and operators cannot see where value currently sits or where it became interrupted.
leveragePoints.result: Acting here can improve member transparency, supply better outcome information, expose at-risk value earlier, and reduce avoidable handoffs and delays.
leveragePoints.classification: Abson: Design · Meadows: #6 information flows; #9 delays
leveragePoints.dependency: Requires event connectivity, common definitions, and permissioned identity resolution.

leveragePoints.title: Decisioning based on realized outcomes
leveragePoints.mechanism: Feed realization, failure, and recovery outcomes—not only impressions or activations—back into future decisions.
leveragePoints.signal: Offer and opportunity decisions remain incomplete if the system learns only that something was shown or activated, rather than whether value was actually realized.
leveragePoints.result: Acting here can improve future relevance, timing, eligibility, and delivery decisions using evidence from completed member outcomes.
leveragePoints.classification: Abson: Feedbacks + Design · Meadows: #7 reinforcing feedback; #6 information flows
leveragePoints.dependency: Requires outcome attribution and an operating process that acts on learning.

leveragePoints.title: Exception detection and recovery
leveragePoints.mechanism: Identify at-risk value, diagnose the interruption, resolve or route it, verify realization, and capture the result.
leveragePoints.signal: Failures currently reduce value realization and trust, but each detected and resolved failure can also become information for future improvement.
leveragePoints.result: Acting here can restore individual value, reduce unresolved exceptions, strengthen trust, and generate evidence about recurring breakdowns.
leveragePoints.classification: Abson: Feedbacks + Design · Meadows: #8 balancing feedback; #6 information flows; #5 rules; #9 delays
leveragePoints.dependency: Requires resolution authority, ownership, partner and service integration, and safeguards against false intervention.

leveragePoints.title: Realized value as the system goal
leveragePoints.mechanism: Align measures and decision rules around appropriate member value realization rather than value issued, activity alone, or breakage.
leveragePoints.signal: Local teams can optimize offers, points issuance, redemption, or service metrics while worthwhile value continues to disappear across the total journey.
leveragePoints.result: Acting here can align discovery, fulfilment, recovery, decisioning, and measurement around the same member outcome.
leveragePoints.dependency: Requires executive alignment and economic validation; a product cannot impose this system goal alone.

productDefinition.title: A transparent rewards experience with visible tracking and recovery
productDefinition.visionStatement: Enable every member to reliably turn worthwhile reward opportunities into value they can see, trust, and use.
productDefinition.oneSentence: A digital rewards experience that helps loyalty-program members discover worthwhile opportunities, see where promised value stands, and initiate or approve recovery when it is delayed, missing, or at risk.
productDefinition.primaryUser: Loyalty-program members with worthwhile, eligible reward value already in motion and a detectable risk that some of it may be delayed, missed, or lost because of a qualification, posting, redemption, fulfilment, partner, or service breakdown.
productDefinition.primaryUserNote: Risk-state segment—not an attitude-based persona. Initial cohort and reward journey still to be validated.
productDefinition.coreJob: Help me receive and use the worthwhile reward value I was promised—and recover it without diagnosing the system or repeatedly chasing support when something breaks.

capabilities.name: Discover
capabilities.description: Surface worthwhile, attainable reward opportunities that a member can understand and act upon.

capabilities.name: Track
capabilities.description: Make qualification, earning, posting, redemption, fulfilment, and unresolved states visible.

capabilities.name: Assure and recover
capabilities.description: Detect at-risk value, intervene or route it, and verify that promised value was realized.

capabilities.name: Learn
capabilities.description: Use realized, failed, and recovered outcomes to improve future decisions and system performance.

wedge.name: Proactive Value Assurance and Recovery
wedge.definition: Monitor worthwhile reward opportunities as they progress from qualification through earning, redemption, and fulfilment; identify when promised value is delayed, missing, or at risk; and either resolve the issue automatically or route it to the responsible service pathway with the necessary context. Members remain informed and retain approval over consequential actions, while recovery outcomes help identify and prevent recurring sources of value loss.
rationale: It directly addresses preventable loss after worthwhile value enters the chain.
It creates an observable member outcome—not only an internal analytical capability.
It can start with one bounded reward journey or failure type and expand over time.

measures.name: Opportunity capture rate
measures.calculation: Points successfully earned ÷ points available through worthwhile, eligible opportunities entering the chain
measures.reveals: How effectively worthwhile earning potential progresses into confirmed earned value

measures.name: Earned-value realization rate
measures.calculation: Earned points successfully converted into fulfilled benefits ÷ earned points available for intended use
measures.reveals: How effectively earned value progresses through visibility, redemption, and fulfilment

measures.name: End-to-end realization rate
measures.calculation: Points-derived value successfully realized ÷ worthwhile, eligible points-value entering the chain
measures.reveals: The conversion efficiency of the complete pathway from worthwhile opportunity to fulfilled benefit

boundary.inScope: Opportunity discovery; value-status visibility; at-risk value detection; member communication and approval; recovery or accountable routing; and outcome verification.
boundary.outOfScope: Replacing loyalty, banking, partner, or service systems; maximizing redemption at any cost; treating intentional saving or informed rejection as value loss; forcing banking conversion; or masking structural failures through repeated case-by-case recovery.

productDefinition.channelAssumption: Embedded within existing authenticated BMO and Blue Rewards digital touchpoints, connecting to current loyalty, banking, partner, and service systems rather than replacing them. The initial channel and role of mobile still need validation.

submissions.behaviourOfInterest: How the loyalty system can direct relevant value toward what members are actually trying to achieve, rather than toward generic reward activity.

leveragePoints.title: Reorient the system around member goal achievement
leveragePoints.mechanism: Set member goal achievement as the system's organizing objective and measure performance through worthwhile, realized value. Members state goals and preferences; BMO combines those signals with observed behaviour to prioritize rewards, experiences and suitable banking products that advance each job.
leveragePoints.signal: Need-based segments provide the starting structure; continued learning can move personalization toward a segment of one.
leveragePoints.result: Goal setup, progress tracking, opportunity ranking and coordinated loyalty-and-banking recommendations would operationalize the change.
leveragePoints.classification: Meadows: #3 system goals — very high leverage
leveragePoints.evidence: Deloitte found loyalty programs increased perceived value for 80% of members, yet consumers actively used only five of eight enrolled programs, supporting a sharper focus on useful value.

leveragePoints.title: Make CDB value visible before asking members to connect accounts
leveragePoints.mechanism: Use a concrete, immediate member benefit as the entry point to consumer-driven banking. Blue Rewards shows how connecting an account may uncover eligible spending, improve reward recommendations or reveal a faster path toward a stated goal. A value preview, followed by a linking incentive or immediately useful insight, gives members a reason to participate.
leveragePoints.signal: The request should then explain what data BMO needs, what additional value it enables and how access can be changed or withdrawn.
leveragePoints.result: Combines a compelling hook with progressive consent, helping R5 gain enough participation to produce useful experiences and visible proof.
leveragePoints.classification: Meadows: #6 information flows; #5 rules of the system — high leverage

leveragePoints.title: Restructure fragmented data and channels into an ambient loyalty experience
leveragePoints.effect: Acts across R4, B2 and R5
leveragePoints.mechanism: Connect member goals and preferences with Blue Rewards activity, BMO relationship data, authorized cross-bank data, digital-intent signals and ISO 20022 payment information. These flows surface opportunities through BMO channels, wallets, approved external services and participating retailers.
leveragePoints.signal: At purchase, members could compare offers, redemption options, payment methods and suitable BMO products against their goal. Merchant and RTR integrations could confirm qualifying payments, update rewards and resolve missing value.
leveragePoints.result: Canada's CDB framework, Google's UK portability rules and loyalBe demonstrate enabling models. An April 2027 capstone would let BMO test consent and decision rules before broader adoption.
leveragePoints.classification: Meadows: #6 information flows, supported by #5 rules of the system — high leverage

divergences.title: What organizes the system: delivered outcome or stated intent?

positions.position: Member value realization — did the worthwhile value the member was promised actually get delivered and become usable? Measurable from system events without asking the member anything.
Member goal achievement — did the member advance the goal they set? Requires the member to state a goal, and requires consent to combine data against it.

divergences.whyItMatters: These are close enough to be mistaken for the same idea and different enough to produce different products. Realization can be measured passively; goal achievement cannot. Adopting Josh's objective adds a member-input dependency, a consent dependency, and a cold-start problem for members who never set a goal. Adopting Sly's leaves the system unable to distinguish value the member wanted from value the member merely received.
resolutionOptions: Treat realization as the measurable proxy and goal achievement as the intent it serves — nest rather than choose.
Adopt goal achievement as the system goal and accept the member-input dependency.
Keep both and test whether goal-setters behave differently from non-goal-setters.
divergences.recommendedNext: Nesting is the least destructive option and preserves both contributors' reasoning, but it must be tested against the cold-start case rather than assumed.

divergences.title: Where the product starts: protect value in motion, or direct value toward goals?

positions.position: Start at the end of the chain. Wedge = Proactive Value Assurance and Recovery: detect at-risk value, resolve or route it, verify realization.
Start at the front of the chain. Emphasis on goal-linked opportunity surfacing and comparison at the moment of decision. (Wedge inferred, not stated — needs Josh's confirmation.)

divergences.whyItMatters: Both models describe the same end-to-end product surface, but enter it from opposite ends. The choice determines the first cohort (members with value at risk vs. members with a stated goal), the first journey, the first metric, and what the team can demonstrate at the capstone.
resolutionOptions: Recovery first — narrower, has a detectable trigger, produces an observable member outcome without needing goals.
Discovery first — broader reach, but depends on goal capture and consent landing first.
Sequence explicitly: recovery proves reliability, then goals direct relevance.
divergences.recommendedNext: Confirm with Josh whether JPM03 is genuinely his intended starting point before treating this as a real disagreement — the inference may be wrong.

divergences.title: Boundary conflict: is consumer-driven banking inside the system?

positions.position: Boundary covers the loyalty program, its partners, and its service pathways. No CDB, cross-bank data, or payment-rail variable exists in the model.
Boundary includes consumer-driven banking, authorized cross-bank data, ISO 20022 payment information, RTR and merchant integrations.

divergences.whyItMatters: This is not a difference of opinion inside one system — the two contributors are modelling systems of different size. Merging nodes and relationships across a boundary mismatch produces a map that is internally inconsistent, which is why this blocks the structural merge rather than merely qualifying it.
resolutionOptions: Adopt the wider boundary and add CDB constructs to the shared map as hypothesis-status.
Keep the narrower boundary and record CDB as an external influence outside it.
Model CDB as a named future-state extension with its own view.
divergences.recommendedNext: Settle this before merging any nodes or relationships. Sly's V2 contract already has a boundary section and an 'Outside the Boundary' view that can hold the wider constructs without committing to them.

divergences.title: Is personalization learning reinforcing or balancing?

positions.position: Learning from realized outcomes sits inside R1 and compounds — better outcomes produce better information, which produces better decisions.
Personalization learning is attached to B2 — Personalized Value & Breakage — a balancing loop that would stabilise rather than compound.

divergences.whyItMatters: The same mechanism cannot be both without a difference somewhere in the link polarities. At least one loop is mis-specified, or the two are describing different mechanisms under similar names.
resolutionOptions: Obtain Josh's B2 structure and compare polarity by polarity.
Determine whether Josh's 'breakage' term introduces a negative link Sly's model does not have.

divergences.title: Evidence asymmetry between submissions

positions.position: Cites external sources: Deloitte loyalty research, Canada's CDB framework, Google's UK portability rules, loyalBe.
One internal contract source; most claims are legacy evidence synthesis or analytical inference with source traceability still pending.

divergences.whyItMatters: Where the two models overlap, Josh's citations must not silently promote Sly's shared claims to 'supported'. The classification model already forbids this, but a merge performed carelessly would do it anyway.
resolutionOptions: Register Josh's sources in the contract's sources array and attach them only to the specific claims they support.
Leave shared claims at their lower epistemic status until independently evidenced.
divergences.recommendedNext: Register the sources; do not let overlap inherit them.
